newsitem.title: ITALY: Four of 10 abducted Italians freed in Yemen.
newsitem.headline: Four of 10 abducted Italians freed in Yemen.

text.p: Four of the 10 Italian tourists who were kidnapped in separate incidents in Yemen this week were set free on Friday, the Italian Foreign Ministry said.

The group of four from the northern town of Cuneo, who were abducted on Thursday morning near Khamir some 100 km (60 miles) north of the capital Sanaa, were taken to the Italian embassy in the capital after their release, the ministry said in a statement.
The statement, which gave no further details, said the tourists were likely to return home in the coming days.

Italian news agency ANSA quoted relatives of the released tourists, who were in their late 20s and early 30s, as saying their kidnappers had treated them very well, giving them whiskey and traditional pastries.
"I'm calm now it seems everything has turned out all right," Liliana Radonia, whose son Franco was among the four, told ANSA.
"My husband had told them that Yemen could be dangerous, but they went ahead and left any way," she said. "Now they will have some adventures to talk about."
Another six Italians from the southern port city of Naples remained in captivity after their abduction on Wednesday while on their way to Al Mukallaa on the Gulf of Aden coast.
The group of six, which included the brother of a former parliamentarian and two children aged nine and 10, had been taken to the interior of the country.
The kidnappings were the latest in a series carried out by Yemeni tribesmen in one of the Arab world's poorest countries.

An Italian kidnapped earlier this month was released last Sunday and two others who were abducted in late July were freed after one day. In March, 11 Germans including seven motorcycle tourists were abducted and later freed.

The tribesmen have tried to use hostages -- who have included French and U.S. diplomats and a Saudi ambassador -- as bargaining chips in land and water disputes with the government and foreign oil firms.
All hostages have so far been released unharmed. Giorgio Gonanomi, the Italian released last Sunday, said he had been fed exotic fruits and treated wonderfully during his five days in captivity.
